title: LexInfo + OntoLex-Lemon Schema Terms

LexInfo + OntoLex-Lemon Schema Terms

This MASP Schema was auto-generated from three merged ontologies using the scripts/owl-to-masp.py script (see spec: "Merging multiple ontologies into one schema"): the LexInfo ontology (v3.0), and the OntoLex-Lemon ontolex (core) and synsem modules that LexInfo's own properties specialise. Converting all three together, rather than as three separate schemas, means classes like ontolex:LexicalEntry and ontolex:LexicalSense — which many LexInfo properties point at as their domain — resolve to real, documented classes here instead of bare external IRIs.

The ontologies' named individuals (e.g. the lexinfo:PartOfSpeech values lexinfo:noun, lexinfo:verb, or the lexinfo:Case, lexinfo:Gender and lexinfo:Tense values) are ported as instances of their class and listed in an ItemList per class. Properties whose range is one of those classes (e.g. lexinfo:partOfSpeech) offer the standard values from that list, but keep the class in their range too, so other instances of the class are still valid.

  • lexical concept — A lexical concept represents a mental abstraction, concept or unit of thought that embodies the meaning of one or more lexical entries.
  • lexical entry — A lexical entry represents a unit of analysis of the lexicon that consists of a set of forms that are grammatically related and a set of base meanings that are associated with all of these forms. Thus, a lexical entry is a word, multiword expression or affix with a single part-of-speech, morphological pattern, etymology and set of senses.
  • lexical sense — A lexical sense represents the lexical meaning of a lexical entry when interpreted as referring to the corresponding ontology element. A lexical sense thus represents a reification of a pair of a uniquely determined lexical entry and a uniquely determined ontology entity it refers to. A link between a lexical entry and an ontology entity via a Lexical Sense object implies that the lexical entry can be used to refer to the ontology entity in question.

  • morphological root — A root is the portion of a word that (a) is common to a set of derived or inflected forms, (b) is not further analyzable into meaningful elements, and (c) carries the principle portion of meaning of the words in which it functions (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/root).
  • morphological stem — A stem is the root or roots of a word, together with any derivational affixes, to which inflectional affixes are added (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/stem). A stem consists minimally of a root, but may be analyzable into a root plus derivational morphemes.
  • multi-word expression — A multiword expression is a lexical entry that consists of two or more words.

  • transfix — A transfix is a discontinuous affix that disrupts the base to which it is attached. The term is reserved for true single affixes, rather than combinations of an infix with an independent prefix or suffix. (Broselow, E., 2000. Transfixation. In G. Booij, et al. (eds.), Ein internationales Handbuch zur Flexion und Wortbildung. 1. Halbband. Mouton De Gruyter, New York, Berlin, p. 552-557.) Examples include discontinuous affixes inserted into a word root, as in root-and-pattern systems of several Semitic languages, e.g., in the Arabic word kitaba "writing" from the root k-t-b.

Properties from adjective

No properties defined directly on this class

Properties from lexical entry

Property Required Description Range Value
abbreviationFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between an abbreviation and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
acronymFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between an acronym and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
canonicalForm No The 'canonical form' property relates a lexical entry to its canoncical or dictionary form. This usually indicates the "lemma" form of a lexical entry. form
clippedTermFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between a clipped term and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
contractionFor No The full form that corresponds to a contracted form. lexical entry
denotes No The 'denotes' property relates a lexical entry to a predicate in a given ontology that represents its meaning and has some denotational or model-theoretic semantics. Resource
derivedForm No A form that is derived morphosyntactically from another form lexical entry
etymologicalRoot No Morpheme that has a particular status with regards to the word's etymology. lexical entry
evokes No The 'evokes' property relates a lexical entry to one of the lexical concepts it evokes, i.e. the mental concept that speakers of a language might associate when hearing the lexical entry. lexical concept
fullFormFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between any full form of a term or lexical unit and its abbreviated form. lexical entry
geographicalVariant No Description of a specific form used in a certain region as opposed to another form used in another region lexical entry
head No Indicates the head element of a phrase lexical entry
homograph No A word that is spelled like another, but that has a different pronunciation, meaning, and/or origin. // Word that is written like another, but that has a different pronunciation, meaning, and/or origin. lexical entry
homonym No A word that is pronounced like another word and that can be spelled the same way (homograph) or can merely sound the same (homophone). // Word that sounds the same and is written the same as another word but is different in meaning. lexical entry
homophone No A word that is pronounced in the same way as another word but that is spelled differently. // Word that sounds like another word, but is different in writiing or meaning. lexical entry
initialismFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between an initialism and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
lexicalForm No The 'lexical form' property relates a lexical entry to one grammatical form variant of the lexical entry. form
morphologicalPattern No The 'morphological pattern' property indicates the morphological class of a word.
otherForm No The 'other form' property relates a lexical entry to a non-preferred ("non-lemma") form that realizes the given lexical entry. form
participleFormOf No Indicates that one lexical entry is the participle form of another, e.g., the adjective 'reassuring' is the participle of 'to reassure' lexical entry
root No base of a word lexical entry
sense No The 'sense' property relates a lexical entry to one of its lexical senses. lexical sense
shortFormFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between a short form and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
synBehavior No The 'syntactic behavior' property relates a lexical entry to one of its syntactic behaviors as captured by a syntactic frame. Syntactic Frame

Class: morphological root (http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#RootMorph)

A root is the portion of a word that (a) is common to a set of derived or inflected forms, (b) is not further analyzable into meaningful elements, and (c) carries the principle portion of meaning of the words in which it functions (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/root).

Class: simulfix (http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#SimulfixMorph)

A simulfix is a change or replacement of vowels or consonants (usually vowels) which changes the meaning of a word (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/simulfix). Examples include umlaut in Germanic languages, e.g., in the formation of the English plural feet from the singular foot.

Class: morphological stem (http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#StemMorph)

A stem is the root or roots of a word, together with any derivational affixes, to which inflectional affixes are added (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/stem). A stem consists minimally of a root, but may be analyzable into a root plus derivational morphemes.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Class: transfix (http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#TransfixMorph)

A transfix is a discontinuous affix that disrupts the base to which it is attached. The term is reserved for true single affixes, rather than combinations of an infix with an independent prefix or suffix. (Broselow, E., 2000. Transfixation. In G. Booij, et al. (eds.), Ein internationales Handbuch zur Flexion und Wortbildung. 1. Halbband. Mouton De Gruyter, New York, Berlin, p. 552-557.) Examples include discontinuous affixes inserted into a word root, as in root-and-pattern systems of several Semitic languages, e.g., in the Arabic word kitaba "writing" from the root k-t-b.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count

Class: zero morph (http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#ZeroMorph)

A zero morph is a morph, consisting of no phonetic form, that is proposed in some analyses as an allomorph of a morpheme that is ordinarily realized by a morph having some phonetic form (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/zero-morph). Examples include the English plural sheep along with the singular sheep.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count
N/A N/A

Properties from form

Property Required Description Range Value
formCaseVariant No form
formDegreeVariant No form
formMoodVariant No form
formNegativeVariant No form
formNumberVariant No form
formPersonVariant No form
formTenseVariant No form
phoneticRep No The 'phonetic representation' property indicates one phonetic representation of the pronunciation of the form using a scheme such as the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). langString
representation No The 'representation' property indicates a string by which the form is represented according to some orthography. langString
writtenRep No The 'written representation' property indicates the written representation of a form. langString

Class: lexical concept (http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalConcept)

A lexical concept represents a mental abstraction, concept or unit of thought that embodies the meaning of one or more lexical entries.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count
N/A N/A

Properties from lexical concept

Property Required Description Range Value
isConceptOf No This property formalizes the meaning of a Lexical Concept by linking it to a particular ontological meaning.
isEvokedBy No The inverse relation to evokes. lexical entry
lexicalizedSense No The 'lexicalized sense' property relates a lexical concept to a corresponding lexical sense that lexicalizes the concept. lexical sense

Class: lexical entry (http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry)

A lexical entry represents a unit of analysis of the lexicon that consists of a set of forms that are grammatically related and a set of base meanings that are associated with all of these forms. Thus, a lexical entry is a word, multiword expression or affix with a single part-of-speech, morphological pattern, etymology and set of senses.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count
N/A N/A

Properties from lexical entry

Property Required Description Range Value
abbreviationFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between an abbreviation and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
acronymFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between an acronym and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
canonicalForm No The 'canonical form' property relates a lexical entry to its canoncical or dictionary form. This usually indicates the "lemma" form of a lexical entry. form
clippedTermFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between a clipped term and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
contractionFor No The full form that corresponds to a contracted form. lexical entry
denotes No The 'denotes' property relates a lexical entry to a predicate in a given ontology that represents its meaning and has some denotational or model-theoretic semantics. Resource
derivedForm No A form that is derived morphosyntactically from another form lexical entry
etymologicalRoot No Morpheme that has a particular status with regards to the word's etymology. lexical entry
evokes No The 'evokes' property relates a lexical entry to one of the lexical concepts it evokes, i.e. the mental concept that speakers of a language might associate when hearing the lexical entry. lexical concept
fullFormFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between any full form of a term or lexical unit and its abbreviated form. lexical entry
geographicalVariant No Description of a specific form used in a certain region as opposed to another form used in another region lexical entry
head No Indicates the head element of a phrase lexical entry
homograph No A word that is spelled like another, but that has a different pronunciation, meaning, and/or origin. // Word that is written like another, but that has a different pronunciation, meaning, and/or origin. lexical entry
homonym No A word that is pronounced like another word and that can be spelled the same way (homograph) or can merely sound the same (homophone). // Word that sounds the same and is written the same as another word but is different in meaning. lexical entry
homophone No A word that is pronounced in the same way as another word but that is spelled differently. // Word that sounds like another word, but is different in writiing or meaning. lexical entry
initialismFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between an initialism and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
lexicalForm No The 'lexical form' property relates a lexical entry to one grammatical form variant of the lexical entry. form
morphologicalPattern No The 'morphological pattern' property indicates the morphological class of a word.
otherForm No The 'other form' property relates a lexical entry to a non-preferred ("non-lemma") form that realizes the given lexical entry. form
participleFormOf No Indicates that one lexical entry is the participle form of another, e.g., the adjective 'reassuring' is the participle of 'to reassure' lexical entry
root No base of a word lexical entry
sense No The 'sense' property relates a lexical entry to one of its lexical senses. lexical sense
shortFormFor No A linking element used to identify a relation between a short form and its full or expanded form. lexical entry
synBehavior No The 'syntactic behavior' property relates a lexical entry to one of its syntactic behaviors as captured by a syntactic frame. Syntactic Frame

Class: lexical sense (http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense)

A lexical sense represents the lexical meaning of a lexical entry when interpreted as referring to the corresponding ontology element. A lexical sense thus represents a reification of a pair of a uniquely determined lexical entry and a uniquely determined ontology entity it refers to. A link between a lexical entry and an ontology entity via a Lexical Sense object implies that the lexical entry can be used to refer to the ontology entity in question.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count
N/A N/A

Properties from lexical sense

Property Required Description Range Value
antonym No A term or lexeme whose concept or sense constitutes the opposite of the concept represented by a second term or lexeme. lexical sense
approximate No Property used to qualify something similar but not exactly the same lexical sense
approximateSynonym No A synonym that differs in some minor way lexical sense
associativeRelation No A relation between two concepts having a non-hierarchical thematic connection by virtue of experience. lexical sense
causallyRelatedConcept No A concept that is related to another concept by virtue of the fact that it plays a causative role with respect to that concept. lexical sense
collocation No Two terms that occur together far more frequently than chance lexical sense
coordinateConcept No A subordinate concept having the same nearest superordinate concept and same criterion of subdivision as some other concept in a given concept system. lexical sense
exact No Completely equal in every detail lexical sense
holonymTerm No Indicates that the referenced element is a part of this object lexical sense
hypernym No A term with a broader meaning lexical sense
hyponym No A term with a narrower meaning lexical sense
isLexicalizedSenseOf No The object property isLexicalizedSenseOf is the inverse property of lexicalized sense. lexical concept
isSenseOf No The property isSenseOf is the inverse property of sense. lexical entry
memberHolonym No Indicates the object is a member of this lexical sense
memberMeronym No Indicates this is an element of the other lexical sense
meronymTerm No Indicates this is a part of another concept lexical sense
ontoCorrespondence No The 'ontoCorrespondence' property binds an argument of a predicate defined in the ontology to a syntactic argument that realizes this predicate argument syntactically. Syntactic Argument
partHolonym No Indicates a part of this object lexical sense
partMeronym No Indicates this a component of the other concept lexical sense
partitiveRelation No A relation between two concepts where one of the concepts constitutes the whole and the other concept a part of that whole. lexical sense
pertainsTo No Indicates that a term is the adjectival form of a word with a meaning of 'of or pertaining to X' lexical sense
quasiEquivalent No A term that is very similar but with some differences lexical sense
reference No The 'reference' property relates a lexical sense to an ontological predicate that represents the denotation of the corresponding lexical entry. Resource
relatedTerm No A term connected to another term by a coordinate or associative relation. lexical sense
substanceHolonym No Indicates what this is composed of lexical sense
substanceMeronym No Indicates this is a substance that composes the other lexical sense
synonym No Indicates the the terms have the same meaning lexicographically lexical sense
translation No Indicates that two terms are translations of one another; this is the same as interlingual synonymy lexical sense
usage No The 'usage' property indicates usage conditions or pragmatic implications when using the lexical entry to refer to the given ontological meaning. Resource

Class: ontology mapping (http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#OntoMap)

An 'ontology mapping' (OntoMap for short) specifies how a syntactic frame and its syntactic arguments map to a set of concepts and properties in the ontology that together specify the meaning of the syntactic frame.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count
N/A N/A

Properties from ontology mapping

Property Required Description Range Value
condition No The 'condition' property defines an evaluable constraint that derives from using a certain lexical entry to express a given ontological predicate.
ontoCorrespondence No The 'ontoCorrespondence' property binds an argument of a predicate defined in the ontology to a syntactic argument that realizes this predicate argument syntactically. Syntactic Argument
ontoMapping No The 'ontoMapping' property relates an ontology mapping to its corresponding lexical sense. lexical sense
reference No The 'reference' property relates a lexical sense to an ontological predicate that represents the denotation of the corresponding lexical entry. Resource
submap No The 'submap' property relates a (complex) ontological mapping to a set of bindings that together bind the arguments of the involved predicates to a set of syntactic arguments that realize them syntactically. ontology mapping

Class: Syntactic Argument (http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticArgument)

A 'syntactic argument' represents a slot that needs to be filled for a certain syntactic frame to be complete. Syntactic arguments typically realize a certain grammatical function (e.g. subject, direct object, indirect object, prepositional object, etc.).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count
N/A N/A

Properties from Syntactic Argument

Property Required Description Range Value
marker No The 'marker' property indicates the marker of a syntactic argument; this can be a case marker or some other lexical entry such as a preposition or particle.
optional No The 'optional' property indicates whether a syntactic argument is optional, that is, it can be syntactically omitted. schema:Boolean

Class: Syntactic Frame (http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticFrame)

A 'syntactic frame' represents the syntactic behavior of an open class word in terms of the (syntactic) arguments it requires. It essentially describes the so called subcategorization structure of the word in question, in particular the syntactic arguments it requires.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

Min Count Max Count
N/A N/A

Properties from Syntactic Frame

Property Required Description Range Value
synArg No The object property synArg relates a syntactic frame to one of its syntactic arguments. Syntactic Argument
